sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Backdrop and centered dialog box
sections.what: Builds the dark layer behind the dialog and the centered box that holds the content. The box includes a close X button in its top right corner, shown on every dialog automatically.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives every pop-up the same backdrop, placement, and close control.
sections.watch_out: Changing this box affects every dialog in the app at once.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Header, footer, title, and description
sections.what: Builds the top area with the title and description, the bottom area for action buttons, and the text styles for each. The layout changes between phone and wide screens.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives dialogs a consistent header and button row.

sections.name: File setup (part 3)
sections.title: Export list
sections.what: Lists the dialog parts so other screens can import and use them.
sections.why: Likely reason: makes the parts available to the rest of the app.

summary: Builds the pop-up dialog pieces: a dark backdrop, a centered box with a close button, a header, a footer, a title, and a description.
purpose: Gives every pop-up window in the app the same look and close button. Other screens put their own content inside these parts.
why: Likely reason: a shared look for dialogs keeps the app consistent. The code does not state this directly.
how: It imports the base dialog library and style helper. It gives each base part a Dialog name. It wraps the backdrop and the content box, and adds a close X button inside the box automatically. It then adds header, footer, title, and description layouts, and exports them all.
inputs: Whether the dialog is open (set by the screen), the content placed inside, optional style overrides, and standard element settings.
outputs: Components that show a modal dialog on top of the page. Nothing is stored.
risks: The library handles focus trapping and closing with the Escape key. Changing the backdrop or content box style affects every dialog in the app. The word Close is only for screen readers and is not visible.
debug: If a dialog does not open, check the screen that controls its open state. If it sits behind other content, check the layer values in this file. If the close X is missing, check the content box wrapper.
